title: Publish model signature + affinity routes API for onboarding and pinning
creator: Ava Patel
description: Purpose: Define and publish a compact, forward-compatible API surface that exposes model signatures (input types, streaming support, function-calling capability, max_context_tokens, supported precisions, kv-cache behavior) and an affinity routing contract used by the router to bind requests to pinned model versions. This ticket covers the schema changes, backwards compatibility constraints, and a lightweight discovery endpoint for customers and internal services to consume during onboarding and runtime routing.
acceptance_criteria: 1) /v1/models/{model}/signature returns a documented JSON schema with fields: display_name, stable_version_tag, available_versions[], max_context_tokens, streaming: boolean, function_calling: enum, kv_cache: {supported: boolean, eviction_policy: string}, precisions: list, recommended_batch_size. 2) /v1/models/{model}/affinity returns routing hints: version_affinity_map, compatibility_matrix, fallback_chain. 3) Response sizes capped to avoid large manifests (<= 32KB). 4) Old clients gracefully ignore extra fields (forward compatible). 5) Unit tests + contract tests + two end-to-end onboarding flows (open model and customer-registered model).
design_decisions:
- Use a shallow, typed envelope (not full nested manifests) to keep discovery cheap.
- Expose stable_version_tag for pin-by-default use cases, and a separate available_versions list for explicit pinning.
- Affinity uses a prioritized list (fallback_chain) instead of a boolean multi-affinity to keep routing deterministic.
- Represent function_calling as enum {none, simple, full} to communicate surface area without leaking impl details.
tradeoffs:
- Pros: Small discovery payload, easier to cache, simpler client logic.
- Cons: Less expressive than full manifest v2; some advanced runtime hints (per-layer kernel preferences) are intentionally omitted and kept internal.
- We accept this tradeoff to favor stability and lower bandwidth for client discovery during onboarding.
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Initial proposal authored and synced with PM (Confluence: /confluence/redwood/model-onboarding/signature-proposal).
2026-03-11: Proto-schema sketched and shared with runtime team; preliminary contract tests added to infra. (See PR #2345).
2026-03-12: Security review questionnaire submitted; pointed out KMS metadata must not be exported in public discovery responses. Updated schema to redact sensitive fields.
2026-03-13: API spec moved to in-review; awaiting infra review and product approval. Added fallback_chain semantics after discussion with routing team.
next_steps: Address infra feedback on response size and add gzip support for large manifests
Add contract test that simulates a client older than schema version and verifies forward-compatibility
Schedule API review with PM and Security (target 2026-03-15)
qa_plan: 1) Unit tests for schema validation and serialization. 2) Contract tests against simulated router and legacy client. 3) End-to-end onboarding test: upload model manifest -> published signature -> route pinned request to expected version. 4) Load test to ensure discovery endpoint can handle 1000 QPS with median latency < 30ms.
notes:
- Security called out that KMS identifiers and customer metadata must be available only through authorized private endpoints; public signature endpoint must never return keys or internal URIs.
- PM requested we surface recommended_batch_size and observed_latency_percentiles in the next iteration but agreed to defer to a follow-up ticket to keep this rollout small.
estimated_risks: 1) Inaccurate signature data could cause client misbehavior (bad batching or out-of-context requests). 2) Large manifests might strain control plane; we mitigate by size cap and gzip. 3) Miscommunication of affinity semantics could cause traffic to be routed to slower variants; mitigate via staged canaries and explicit fallback tests.
review_feedback:
- Design: prefer enum for function_calling to boolean (implemented).
- Runtime: requested an explicit field for kv_cache_warmup_hint (string) — added as optional nullable string.
- Security: redact all customer-specific URIs; return 'private_metadata_available': boolean instead.
customer_examples: Example consumer flow: 1) Client calls /v1/models/llama-3/signature -> gets stable_version_tag: 'v2.1.0', max_context_tokens: 32k, function_calling: 'simple'. 2) Client pins to 'v2.1.0' via API or uses affinity routing to prefer v2.1.0 with fallback_chain ['v2.0.5','v1.9.9'].
owner_notes: If infra cannot guarantee the size cap, switch to a paging approach: /signature?page=1 and document stable cursor semantics. Keep the first rollout read-only (no write operations through this API).
